caption: The drawing consists of three pig-shaped objects, each depicted in a different orientation: one is shown in a three-quarter side view (top), one in a direct side profile (middle), and one in a view from below or with legs up (bottom). The pig figures are primarily rendered in shades of gray, with the top pig featuring a slightly more brownish-gray hue, while the other two are lighter, more off-white or pale gray. Each pig's surface is marked with numerous place names, labels, and lines reminiscent of map cartography, written in dark blue or black ink. The place names are distributed evenly across the pigs' bodies, with lines dividing various regions much like a map. The middle pig includes a prominent inscription over the body reading, “St. Louis the Western Metrop [sic] Rail Road & River Guide by Anna Pottery 1889.” The bottom pig, viewed from the underside, also bears names and inscriptions, such as “Cincinnati, the Pork Packing City” and “Chicago the Corn City.” The overall background is a plain, light beige or off-white, with no additional objects or scenery present.
title: Pottery Pig
